How this guide is organised

The specification says what Version 2 must do. This guide is for understanding it. Its pieces don't make sense one at a time: the drawing model only makes sense alongside the document it lives in, and the document only alongside the blocks around it. So the guide goes over the whole thing more than once, each pass closer in:

  1. Part 1, Sketchpad today. How the current program is put together, with diagrams, so the changes have something to be measured against.
  2. Part 2, What gets in the way. The weaknesses, in plain terms, grouped by cause rather than listed by file.
  3. Part 3, The new design from the top down. Three cycles. The first is one picture of the whole. The second names the blocks and what each is for. The third follows three ordinary actions through the blocks. Blocks such as the catalog and storage stop at that level: what they do, not how.
  4. Part 4, The drawing model: a tutorial. The part you will live with. It starts from a single list of points and builds, lesson by lesson, to figures whose layers depend on each other and to writing your own object. Every picture in Part 4 was computed from the rules it illustrates, so what you see is exactly what the rule produces.

Words in this type are names as they would appear in code. The kernel's vocabulary is summarised on the last page for reference while you read.
